text:
### Observed differences

- The three activities A19, A21 and A24 changed their dominant successor from A25 to A30: in the earlier window, about 95–98 in 100 of each one's outgoing transitions went to A25; in the later window, about 95–98 in 100 go to A30. These are the rarer activities (about 60–80 observed outgoing transitions per window, i.e. roughly 30–40 in 100 traces), and their frequency barely moved. [DIR001, DIR003, DIR006]
- The trio A20, A22 and A23 (about 200 observed outgoing transitions per window, i.e. present in nearly every trace) kept passing control among one another at similar shares (roughly 30 in 100 of outgoing transitions to each of the other two, in both windows) but changed its exit: earlier about 29–37 in 100 of outgoing transitions went to A30; in the later window the same share goes to A25, and A30 is no longer observed as their successor. [DIR002, DIR004, DIR005]
- The two bridge activities switched targets: A29's outgoing transitions moved from A20, A23 and A22 (about 37, 33 and 30 in 100) to A24, A19 and A21 (about 38, 32 and 29 in 100); A40's moved from A24, A21 and A19 (about 34, 33 and 28 in 100) to A22, A20 and A23 (about 34, 31 and 28 in 100). [DIR007, DIR008]
- Execution order between the two groups reversed. A20, A22 and A23 co-occur with A25 in essentially every trace in both windows, but A25 ran before them in about 99 in 100 of those traces earlier and after them in about 99 in 100 later; against A29 the direction also flipped (A29 first in about 99 in 100 earlier, last in about 99 in 100 later). [REL008, REL015, REL018, REL009, REL016, REL019]
- Every cross-pair between the group A19/A21/A24 and the activities A20/A22/A23/A25/A29 reversed in the roughly 30–39 of 100 traces where both members occur: for example, A19 ran before A20 in 30 in 100 traces earlier and after it in 33 in 100 later; A21 before A22 in 34 in 100 earlier and after it in 29 in 100 later; A24 before A20 in 36 in 100 earlier and after it in 38 in 100 later; A19 before A29 in 30 in 100 earlier versus A29 before A19 in 33 in 100 later. All 21 relation items show this same reversal. [REL001, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL010, REL014, REL020, REL021]
- Distances changed consistently: A29 reached A30 typically 4 positions later in the earlier window (about 93 in 100 of the pair's within-five-step occurrences) and 2 positions later in the later window (about 99 in 100); A40 reached A25 typically 2 positions earlier versus 4 positions later (about 95 vs 92 in 100). The direct successions A21 then A25 (69 traces) and A24 then A25 (71 traces) at distance 1 shrink to 1–2 traces, while A29 then A21 at distance 1 (58 traces) and A40 then A20/A22/A23 at distances 1–3 (about 200 traces each) appear only in the later window. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two segments of the flow exchanged their execution order. Earlier, the segment containing A19, A21 and A24 — each closing into A25 — ran between A40 and A25, while the segment containing the circulating trio A20, A22 and A23, exiting to A30, ran after A29; in the later window the two segments have exchanged places, so A29 and A40 now lead into the other segment, A19, A21 and A24 end in A30, and the trio exits to A25. Participation of every involved activity is essentially unchanged, so this is a reordering of the flow rather than activities appearing, disappearing or running more or less often. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, REL008, LAG005, LAG009]

The hypothesis is shown directly and consistently: all 21 relation items show clean order reversals, including pairs that co-occur in nearly every trace, so the reversal is not an artifact of rare co-occurrence; all eight successor profiles change in the direction the exchange predicts; and the distance items match quantitatively (A29 to A30 gap 4 to 2, A40 to A25 gap 2 to 4, direct successions appearing and disappearing on the predicted sides). Screening qualified 38 control-flow items against roughly 0.64 expected if nothing had changed — far more than chance produces — and every item's difference exceeds those in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled traces. [REL001, REL008, DIR001, DIR007, LAG004, LAG005, LAG009]

Limitations: most items describe the same underlying rearrangement, so they corroborate one another but are not independent confirmations; and with one window on each side, the evidence cannot distinguish a reordering of the flow from a complete flip in the mix of two pre-existing orders, since each window shows almost exclusively one order (about 99 in 100). [REL008, REL015, REL019]

Other differences: a handful of low-frequency transitions, each about 1–2 in 100 of the source's outgoing transitions, differ between the windows — for example, about 2 in 100 of A19's outgoing transitions went to A18 earlier and to A02 later, and small edges from A24 (to A36, A40, A32, A04) and from A40 (to A10, A06) appear only in the later window. These sit at the edge of observability in 200-trace windows and are not part of the main hypothesis. [DIR001, DIR006, DIR008]
